video_title: Hedgeye Investing Summit Fall 2026 | HAM PMs R. Patrick Kent & Sam Rahman and HAM CIO John McNamara
gist: Keith McCullough and Hedgeye Asset Management PMs Sam Rahman, R. Patrick Kent and CIO John McNamara argue for signal-driven risk management over buy-and-hold. The macro call is late Quad 2 rolling into Quad 4 in 2027, with bearish trends in AI-bubble neoclouds (IREN, CoreWeave, SK Hynix) and strength in refiners, healthcare and cybersecurity. They also cover a short-list shorting discipline and risk-range-based hedged ETFs (S&P, Bitcoin) as an alternative to static buffer products.

insights.claim: Hedgeye's macro view is that the US economy is pushing toward the top-right extreme of Quad 2 (accelerating growth and inflation) and will swing back into Quad 4 in 2027.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Positioning should stay cyclical/Quad 2 for now while preparing hedges and defensive exposure for a 2027 Quad 4 downturn.
insights.quote: we're pushing towards the top right end of the quad 2 uh the top right corner and then we're going to rip back into quad 4 in 2027

insights.claim: Keith McCullough says a bear market is already underway in bonds, as the market sits in Quad 2 with US equities (Nasdaq/Qs) hitting repeated all-time highs.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Avoid long-duration bonds; consider TLT-short style exposure while rates keep grinding higher.

insights.claim: A cited observation: anyone under ~45 is experiencing their first rising-rate environment, which challenges investors whose playbook is triple-levered Nvidia and 0DTE options.
insights.speaker: John McNamara
insights.so_what: Speculative leveraged-beta strategies are untested in a rising-rate regime; favors risk-adjusted/hedged approaches.
insights.quote: if you're under the age of 45 this is the first time in your life you've ever seen a rising rate environment

insights.claim: Traditional low-beta dividend defensives such as consumer staples have been a disaster this year because rising interest rates, driven by structural deficits and spending, hit their bond-proxy dividend component.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: Underweight staples/bond proxies while yields rise; they become usable defensives only once rates top or Quad 4 pulls yields down.

insights.claim: If interest rates top out or Quad 4 arrives and yields pull back, traditional defensives like staples should start working again.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: Watch the rate peak as the trigger to rotate back into staples/low-beta dividend names.

insights.claim: Hedgeye says Fourth Turning-style portfolios should hold opposite Quad 2 and Quad 4 exposures at once, since those quads sit at opposite extremes and the transition is expected.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Barbell cyclical longs with defensive/short exposure rather than betting on one regime.

insights.claim: Hedgeye's 35-name AI-bubble dashboard (slide 141, 'Hedgeye Big Theme') showed 15 of 35 names in bearish trend last week; SK Hynix flipped to bearish within the past 24 hours after Samsung/SK Hynix news.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Memory-chip names are rolling over in the trend signals; avoid or short those breaking trend.
insights.quote: 15 of 35 names are um are bearish

insights.claim: CoreWeave is set to go back on Hedgeye's Signal Strength short list after the SK Hynix blow-up, joining IREN, which is already there; Oracle is also signaling bearish trend.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Lower-quality AI infrastructure names are breaking trend first; candidates for short or avoidance.

insights.claim: IREN is the biggest candidate to be the 'WeWork of data centers': long leases, contracts and not even profitable on an accounting basis, so a demand wobble could take the stock from 35 to 3.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: Asymmetric short candidate if AI compute demand softens; watch leasing economics and demand indicators.
insights.quote: it's the one that is the biggest candidate for like the weiwork of data centers

insights.claim: The neocloud business model exists only because AI compute demand exceeds supply (swing capacity); once capacity catches up, neoclouds become low-margin bare-metal businesses that add no value.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Neoclouds are the lowest-quality, highest balance-sheet-risk tier of the AI buildout and most exposed to a capacity glut.
insights.quote: the Neocloud business model is predicated on the fact that

insights.claim: IREN fell about 12% in the week after Hedgeye's AI bubble presentation.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Early confirmation of the bearish AI-infrastructure call.

insights.claim: Sam Rahman says you can believe the AI bubble will end and still play it long while factors, fundamentals and signals point that way. Like the 1998-99 yellow flags before the Q1 2000 internet peak, current yellow flags don't mean the top is in.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Stay long quality AI growth with trend signals as the exit trigger rather than front-running the top.
insights.quote: There were yellow flags going back to the internet bubble in 99 2000.

insights.claim: Keith McCullough suggested a leaked story that OpenAI is insolvent without raising capital could trigger the Fourth Turning trade (risk-off defensives working).
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: OpenAI funding stress is a potential catalyst for AI-bubble unwind and defensive rotation.

insights.claim: RPK's two cardinal shorting mistakes are 'big game hunting' famous blow-up shorts like Tesla or Carvana, chasing prestige over returns, and 'fire and forget' shorts on a one-line thesis without active management.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: Short the 'wounded zebras' with high turnover and active management rather than crowded heroic shorts.
insights.quote: they're all looking for sort of prestige optimization, not returns

insights.claim: Shorting is by definition a high-velocity, high-turnover strategy; even correct theses must be managed because declines are never a straight line.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: Size and trade shorts actively (cover and press along the trend) rather than holding statically.

insights.claim: Keith McCullough says the top 35 longest-held names on Hedgeye's Signal Strength short list all have positive absolute short returns, mostly double-digit, even as the market made all-time highs.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: The short list is a source of alpha even in a bull tape; RPK draws from it for the HELS/HEFT short books.

insights.claim: Long-held Hedgeye shorts include widely owned names Lululemon, Las Vegas Sands and McDonald's; Domino's Pizza was cited as an analyst-driven short.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Widely held consumer names in bearish trend; a flip to bullish would carry information.

insights.claim: For a long-only manager, names moving off the short list are a signal: Costco recently came off the short list and moved back to the long list after years as a laggard.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Treat short-list exits as potential long entry signals; Costco could become a winner.
insights.quote: Costco being on the short list for quite a while and now it's come off

insights.claim: The Fourth Turning ETF (HEFT) has been only roughly 30-50% net long equities this year, with shorts and downside protection that show up on down days.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: HEFT should not be benchmarked to the S&P; it is a diversified long-term thematic portfolio with hedges.
insights.quote: we've been only like net long equities by about like I don't know between 30 and 50% at any given time this year

insights.claim: Cybersecurity, a long-running Neil Howe Fourth Turning theme, has started working strongly in recent months, though Hedgeye's process was short cyber and software six months ago, so the position was kept small until signals confirmed.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: Core secular themes should be sized up only once quantitative signals confirm the trend.

insights.claim: Healthcare is a core HEFT position on demographic grounds, increased months ago when Hedgeye's signal on healthcare turned more positive.
insights.speaker: R. Patrick Kent (RPK)
insights.so_what: Demographic tailwind plus positive signal supports a healthcare overweight as a defensive growth exposure.

insights.claim: Winning HEFT holdings on a down day included Philip Morris, energy, refiners and software.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: These exposures act as the defensive/Fourth Turning hedge against high-beta selloffs.

insights.claim: The shale revolution flipped WTI from a premium to a discount to Brent, turning US refiners into captive capacity short cheap feedstock and driving a step-change in refiners' return on invested capital.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Refiners carry a structural ROIC advantage in addition to cyclical crack-spread upside.

insights.claim: Valero and Exxon are among the top performers in Sam Rahman's growth strategy, helped by the war, wide crack spreads, and the US having stopped building refinery capacity years ago.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Tight refining capacity sustains crack spreads; macro-aware positioning in refiners has paid.

insights.claim: Keith McCullough argues the best investments are where structural/secular trends meet the cyclical setup and the quant signal confirms it.
insights.speaker: Keith McCullough (host)
insights.so_what: Look for overlap of secular story, cyclical quad tailwind and bullish trend signal before sizing up.
insights.quote: the best investments are when the the structural and secular meets the cyclical

insights.claim: Sam Rahman says exiting stocks quickly when they broke trend in March (Iran war, bottom only in early April) and in July (semiconductor pullback) did better than holding through as a long-term investor.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Even long-term growth investors benefit from trend-break exits; drawdown avoidance compounds.

insights.claim: Sam Rahman says very few investors (Buffett, Ned Johnson) can truly ignore duration because they control their capital. Everyone else, with a 1-3 year view, must navigate short-term drawdowns or risk having nothing left in three years.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Combine long-term theses with short-term risk management; shallow drawdowns allow more frequent all-time highs.

insights.claim: At Fidelity, tax sensitivity meant Sam Rahman couldn't trade in and out around Quad 4, so he focused on one decision with edge: how to position for the exit from Quad 4.
insights.speaker: Sam Rahman
insights.so_what: Tax-constrained investors should use quad forecasts to pre-position for the next regime rather than trade twice.

insights.claim: Hedgeye's hedged S&P and hedged Bitcoin ETFs (including HBIT) can trade options as often as daily using risk-range signals with three-week-or-less duration, unlike buffer/hedged-equity incumbents that use static quarterly strikes set at a fixed percentage of spot.
insights.speaker: John McNamara
insights.so_what: Dynamic hedging should produce variable beta/volatility and better risk-adjusted returns than static buffer products.
insights.quote: Oh I always love it when I can answer a question with the oneliner and it's just the risk range.

insights.claim: John McNamara estimates the hedged-equity ETF category at roughly $80-100B, with some players projecting $600B by 2030, and says it is full of mediocre static strategies.
insights.speaker: John McNamara
insights.so_what: Fast-growing category where risk-adjusted differentiation can win assets; a hedged Bitcoin category barely exists yet.
insights.quote: The last time I looked it was around 80 billion.

insights.claim: A hedged S&P product should not be judged on 1- and 3-year raw returns versus SPY, because dynamic hedging deliberately varies its beta and volatility versus spot.
insights.speaker: John McNamara
insights.so_what: Evaluate hedged products on risk-adjusted metrics and drawdowns, not raw trailing returns in a bull market.
